subject: Post-call recap: scoped TCO levers, procurement timing & pilot commitment
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@ledgerly.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, Dec 1, 2027 at 3:08 PM -0800
Subject: Re: Intro / demo — quick follow-up

Neha / team,

Thanks for the demo today — appreciated the walkthrough. Quick recap from our side and requests so we can move procurement internally: 

- Pain: Our fraud-scrub chatflows are ballooning token spend as we expand event ingestion. We need predictable unit cost and a clear path to <50% WAF (workload-adjusted fees) compared to current hosted model.
- Goal: Proof we can bring per-transaction inference spend under $0.002 (all-in) at scale for our high-throughput validation flows.
- Constraints: Procurement needs a 45-day lead time for any new vendor, and a one-page TCO that ties to our Q1 budget committee.

Can you send the TCO worksheet you mentioned (batching/kv-cache scenarios + SOW sketch) and an ask list we can hand to Procurement? Also please confirm timelines for a 6-week pilot and any required security docs.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Head of Platform Integrations
Ledgerly

Attachments: none on my side (I expect your TCO worksheet).

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, Dec 1, 2027 at 6:35 PM -0800
Subject: Re: Intro / demo — quick follow-up

Julia — great to meet you and thanks for the clear asks. Attaching the TCO-worksheet-v1.xlsx and a short pricing summary (PDF). Quick recap of the call plus the levers we think will matter for Ledgerly's high-throughput fraud flows: 

Recap / pain points we heard:
- High token volume from multi-turn validation + event history rehydration.
- Need deterministic per-transaction cost to satisfy finance and minimize unexpected overages.
- Procurement lead time and SSO/KMS needs are gating for production.

Primary TCO levers and expected impact (rough guidance; will refine with your telemetry):
- Batching (server-side continuous batching): reduces per-token GPU overhead. Estimated savings: 18–32% for typical concurrency we saw in your demo (higher at steady-state).
- Prefix/KV caching (prompt reuse across sessions): can cut prompt-token volume 10–45% depending on reuse patterns — especially for static policy prompts and case-history snippets.
- Model quantization & smaller model routing: route low-risk transactions to a quantized variant — saves 20–40% on compute cost vs full fp16 variants.
- Dedicated capacity option (reserved): moves unit cost predictably down vs burst/hosted; useful if you hit stable throughput during peak windows.

Baseline reference for sizing (from your demo telemetry):
- Current monthly token volume (estimate): ~420M tokens
- Baseline estimated cost (hosted, unoptimized): $27k/month (token+compute estimate) — we'll replace this with precise numbers once we ingest logs.
- Target: sub-$15k/month, with applied batching + caching + routing (~40–55% total savings achievable depending on reuse).

Pilot proposal (6 weeks) — minimal scope to validate economics and latency SLOs:
1) Week 0–1: Access + logs ingestion + shared TCO worksheet population
2) Week 2–3: Batch & cache tuning on a dedicated pool; perf and token-savings monitor
3) Week 4: Canary rollout on 5–10% traffic; latency and error SLOs verification
4) Week 5–6: Full pilot run for final TCO measurement and decision brief

Attachments included: TCO-worksheet-v1.xlsx, redwood-pricing-summary.pdf, redwood-pilot-sow-draft.docx (SOW is a starter draft you can hand to Procurement).

Next steps (action items):
- We (Redwood): finalize TCO numbers after you share anonymized token samples (CSV) — Ben will lead the SOW/pricing follow-up.
- You (Ledgerly): confirm procurement window (you mentioned ~45 days) and share any required legal/infosec docs we should prepare now (SOC2 attestation, KMS details).
- Proposed meeting: Tue, Dec 7 at 10:00 AM PT to review the populated worksheet and SOW.

If that schedule works, Ben and Marissa will prep the SOW and a one-page TCO summary for your Q1 budget packet.

Thanks — attaching the files now.

—
Neha Kapoor
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Intro / demo — scoped TCO levers, procurement timing & pilot commitment

Julia, team — final confirmation and checklist for Procurement and your Budget committee: 

Decision checklist for Pilot go/no-go (we'll deliver a filled checklist at the end of Week 2):
- SSO + minimal legal (NDA executed) — Ledgerly procurement requested: yes/no
- SOC2 report / security package delivered – Redwood to place in Drive link above: yes/no
- 24–48h token sample delivered by Ledgerly: yes/no
- Pilot acceptance: target per-transaction all-in cost <= $0.002 (measured week 5–6): yes/no

Procurement timeline suggestion (to match your 45-day vendor cycle):
- Week A (today): SOW draft in Drive (redwood-pilot-sow-draft.docx) — Ben will iterate
- Week A+1: Procurement reviews, security pack intake
- Week A+3: Contract signature (LOI or MSA) — we can accept a pilot addendum to expedite
- Week A+4: Pilot start (6 weeks) — measurements reported after pilot completes

Quick TCO notes for your budget packet (one-paragraph summary we can use verbatim):
Redwood estimates that with continuous server-side batching, prefix/KV caching, and model-variant routing, Ledgerly can expect 35–50% reduction in inference compute spend compared to a naive hosted configuration. For the sample telemetry shared on the call, that maps to moving from an estimated $27k/month to ~$12–18k/month depending on cache hit rates and batching latency targets. Final numbers will come from the submitted token sample and the populated TCO worksheet.

Proposed next meeting: Tue, Dec 7, 2027 10:00 AM PT — review populated worksheet and sign off on SOW draft. If Procurement prefers a separate intro, we can do a 30-minute procurement-only session that same week.

Please confirm the token-sample delivery ETA and if Dec 7 at 10:00 AM PT works. Once confirmed we'll lock the calendar and Ben will attach the SOW iteration.

Thanks — Neha
—
Neha Kapoor
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
